UNESCO_ICOMOS_2013_1111.organization: ICOMOS via UNESCO World Heritage Centre
UNESCO_ICOMOS_2013_1111.scope: ICOMOS evaluation and technical mission synthesis; regional relationships and documented attributes, not a field survey of component dimensions

UNESCO_PROPERTY_1111.title: Cultural Landscape of Honghe Hani Rice Terraces

system.claim: The regional cultural landscape is a four-part integrated system of forest, water supply, villages/houses, and terraces.
Villages are normally at the top of the terraces below the mountain-top forests.
system.applicable_scope: regional vertical relationship; not an elevation prescription

system.claim: Water-recharge and sacred forests are intensively protected; consolidation forests stabilize steep slopes.
A village-employed forest guard oversees traditional management of sacred and recharge forests.
The property contains 82 villages; most contain 50 to 100 households and each household farms one or two terrace plots.
system.applicable_scope: 2013 property statistics; not a universal settlement module

system.claim: The official property record covers 16,603.22 ha with a 29,501.01 ha buffer zone.
system.applicable_scope: World Heritage property and buffer boundaries; not a generated scene extent

water_distribution.claim: Brooks and springs in and around forests feed a gravity distribution system serving fields and villages.
The documented conveyance family includes dug streams, ditches, canals, and bamboo tubes or pipes.
water_distribution.applicable_scope: object inventory; does not give dimensions or license one form as a default

water_distribution.claim: Four trunk canals and 392 branch ditches total 445.83 km and are maintained communally.
Wood-cuts on posts indicate water need when water is plentiful; scarce water is allocated by taking turns.
water_distribution.applicable_scope: allocation semantics; no instantaneous flow equation is supplied

water_distribution.claim: A village ditch watcher supervises fair distribution and avoids excessive delivery.

terraces.claim: Terraces follow mountain contours and can form up to 3,000 levels between forest edge and valley floor in some places.
terraces.applicable_scope: landscape form; 3,000 is not a per-sample target

terraces.claim: Terraces are constructed from black clay.
The evaluated terraces have no retaining walls; the terrace riser is the cut face of clay.
terraces.applicable_scope: evaluated property; local exceptions require separate evidence

rice.claim: Red rice is the dominant crop and is integrated with cattle, buffalo, pigs, ducks, fish, eels, snails, and vegetables.
rice.applicable_scope: regional farming-system membership, not permission to place every animal in every field

rice.claim: The evaluation records rice cultivation from late April to late September.
rice.applicable_scope: reported regional calendar; exact stage dates remain variety- and altitude-dependent

rice.claim: Farmers select varieties and methods according to local conditions and altitude; the evaluation reports as many as 48 local red-rice varieties.
rice.applicable_scope: diversity constraint; no single generic red-rice morphology

rice.claim: The evaluation reports that hybrid rice does not survive above 1,500 m and is used in some lower terraces.
rice.applicable_scope: statement in the 2013 evaluation; cultivar-specific verification remains required

subregions.claim: The nominated property contains Bada, Duoyishu, and Laohuzui blocks in three different river basins.
Bada is described as gentle, Duoyishu as steeper, and Laohuzui as very steep because of differing geology.
subregions.applicable_scope: relative gradient classes only; no numeric slopes are supplied

terrace_interpretation.exceptions_policy: local stone or other retaining work requires its own site and date evidence

production_gate.reason: official system evidence is usable, but surveyed component dimensions, openings, field sections, crop morphology, and terrain truth are incomplete
